title: UAE Logistics Brief
lede: Gulf crude flows collapsed to about 8.5 million barrels a day last week as Iran stepped up attacks and claimed another tanker hit a mine on the southern route out of Hormuz. On land and in the air the squeeze continues: Etihad has extended its Riyadh and Dammam cancellations to 24 October, while Khor Fakkan races to double capacity for the boxes being pushed to the east coast.

stories.headline: Gulf crude flows crash as Iran claims another tanker hit a mine
body: Kpler puts Gulf crude flows at about 8.5 million barrels a day over the last seven days, down from more than 20 million the week before. On Monday Iran's Revolutionary Guards said a tanker struck a mine and caught fire while leaving by an "unauthorised" southern route with its tracking switched off. The claim has not been verified.

Brent settled at $109.55 on Monday. The GCC says its states have faced more than 7,000 missile and drone attacks since 28 February and wants Hormuz traffic back to pre-war status. Russia's Lavrov was in Tehran on Monday to discuss de-escalation.
stories.soWhat: Iran is warning ships off the very route they use to avoid it. Gulf sea cover and freight costs will stay high this week, so keep war-risk surcharges in place.

stories.headline: Khor Fakkan is doubling capacity to catch boxes pushed to the east coast
body: Gulftainer is investing $2 billion to take Khor Fakkan to 10 million TEUs, with a first phase of 5 million TEUs due by month-end. A new landside gate has lifted weekly throughput from about 8,000 to 65,000 TEUs, with a target of about 100,000 a week. Inland depots at Sajaa and Al Dhaid add 2.3 million TEUs.
Jebel Ali handles about 14–15 million TEUs a year against capacity above 19 million. A study cited by the article says moving freight overland costs 2.4 to 4.2 times more per ton-km.
stories.soWhat: East-coast volume is set to keep growing. Our trucking from Khor Fakkan to Dubai and Abu Dhabi is a product to price for, not a stopgap.

stories.headline: Etihad extends Saudi cancellations to 24 October
body: Etihad has cancelled Abu Dhabi–Riyadh and Abu Dhabi–Dammam flights through Saturday 24 October, a week longer than before. Four Abu Dhabi–Jeddah services (EY601 to EY604) are also cancelled to 24 October. The airline warned of more changes.
Fighting has also grown around the Bab Al Mandab, according to the same report.
stories.soWhat: UAE–KSA belly space will not come back this week as hoped. Keep road as the main KSA product and do not promise air transit times into Riyadh before the weekend.

stories.headline: Al Sharqi opens a Dh70m cold and ambient hub at Dubai Industrial City
body: Al Sharqi Shipping has opened a Dh70 million hub with 280,000 sq ft of storage, 200,000 sq ft of open yard and 22,000 palletised tonnes of storage from ambient to −18°C. It has 38 loading bays and can handle 178 trucks a day. It targets F&B, FMCG, retail, HoReCa, quick commerce and manufacturing.
stories.soWhat: More multi-temperature space near Jebel Ali and Al Maktoum Airport means more choice for food and q-commerce shippers. Expect sharper pricing on contract logistics tenders.

stories.headline: JD.com's property arm plans a 2.5m sq ft Dubai logistics hub
body: Gargash Prime and JINGDONG Property, the infrastructure arm of JD.com, signed an MoU to form a joint venture for a 2.5 million sq ft logistics site in Dubai. It would be a regional distribution and fulfilment hub for the UAE and the Middle East. No investment figure, timeline or tenants were given.
stories.soWhat: Chinese e-commerce players are building their own Gulf fulfilment base. That could pull cross-border volume away from carriers unless we partner early on last mile.

stories.headline: UAE-backed $2.5bn freight railway breaks ground in Jordan
body: The Jordan-UAE Railway Company has started work on the 403 km Aqaba–Al-Shidiyeh–Maan line. It will carry about 16 million tonnes of phosphate and potash a year. Abu Dhabi's L'IMAD Holding holds an equal stake with four Jordanian shareholders, and Etihad Rail brings operating experience. No opening date was given.
stories.soWhat: A long-term play, but it shows UAE money building land corridors that avoid Hormuz. Worth tracking for future Red Sea–Gulf freight routes.

competitors.name: FedEx
competitors.headline: FedEx launches dangerous goods by road across five GCC markets
body: FedEx now carries eligible dangerous goods by road in the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, Kuwait and Oman through its Regional Economy and Regional Economy Freight services. The road network links to its Dubai World Central hub.
That hub gained IATA CEIV Pharma certification on 9 October. It covers 57,000 sq m, with 170 sq m of temperature-controlled storage.
competitors.soWhat: With air into KSA unreliable, FedEx is selling road for the hard-to-move freight too. We need a clear DG road offer and healthcare credentials to defend industrial and pharma accounts.

competitors.name: J&T Express
competitors.headline: J&T's new markets, including the Middle East, grow 160% in Q3
body: J&T moved 9.58 billion parcels in Q3 2026, up 24.8%, or 104.2 million a day. Its Other Markets segment, which covers its newer regions including the Middle East, handled 270.8 million parcels, up 159.5%. The company named the Middle East as a cross-border e-commerce focus. No UAE or Saudi figures were given.
competitors.soWhat: A low-cost, high-volume rival is scaling fast in new markets. Expect more price pressure on marketplace and cross-border B2C parcels in the GCC.

competitors.name: Aramex (baseline)
competitors.headline: No new Aramex announcement since the GMR India MoU
body: Our latest result is still Q2 2026: record revenue of Dh1.83 billion, up 22%, and net profit of Dh47.4 million. EBITDA rose 73% to Dh181.3 million. Gross margin eased to 21.4% from 22%. Freight forwarding had its best quarter ever.
competitors.soWhat: Revenue is growing but margin is slipping. With fuel and war-risk costs still rising, cost recovery in pricing matters more than volume this quarter.

opportunities.title: East-coast trucking as a core product
opportunities.text: Khor Fakkan is heading for 100,000 TEUs a week and 10 million TEUs a year. Regular, priced road capacity to Dubai and Abu Dhabi will be in demand for months.

opportunities.title: KSA road while Etihad stays out to 24 October
opportunities.text: Abu Dhabi–Riyadh and Dammam air is off for another week. Shippers need a reliable road option now.

opportunities.title: Cold-chain and q-commerce contract logistics
opportunities.text: New multi-temperature space at Dubai Industrial City shows demand from F&B and quick commerce. We can bundle storage with last mile.

opportunities.title: Last mile for Chinese e-commerce hubs
opportunities.text: JD's planned 2.5m sq ft Dubai hub will need delivery partners across the UAE and GCC.

opportunities.title: Pharma and DG by road
opportunities.text: FedEx has moved first on DG road in the GCC. Industrial and healthcare shippers will compare offers.

watchouts.title: Southern Hormuz route now targeted
watchouts.text: Iran says a tanker hit a mine on the 'unauthorised' southern route. Cover and carrier caution may spread to east-coast calls.

watchouts.title: Gulf flows fell by more than half in a week
watchouts.text: Kpler's 8.5m barrels a day shows how fast shipping can freeze. Plan for sudden capacity loss.

watchouts.title: Jet fuel still climbing
watchouts.text: Up another 1.2% on the week to $192.44 a barrel. Air fuel surcharges must keep pace.

watchouts.title: Rivals moving on road and pharma
watchouts.text: FedEx DG road in five GCC markets and pharma certification at DWC target our industrial and healthcare base.

watchouts.title: Low-cost parcel rivals scaling
watchouts.text: J&T's new markets grew 160% in Q3. Expect pressure on B2C parcel rates.

moves.title: Keep KSA air off sale until 24 October
moves.text: Etihad has extended Riyadh and Dammam cancellations. Sell road as the default and tell key accounts the new date.

moves.title: Hold war-risk and fuel surcharges
moves.text: Gulf flows crashed and jet fuel rose again. Check our sea war-risk and air fuel recovery against this week's costs before any discounting.

moves.title: Price Khor Fakkan trucking as a standing product
moves.text: Build a published rate card for Khor Fakkan to Dubai and Abu Dhabi with volume tiers, using the port's growth to 100,000 TEUs a week.

moves.title: Build a GCC DG road offer
moves.text: Answer FedEx's DG road launch with our own offer and contact top industrial accounts first.

moves.title: Approach the JD–Gargash project early
moves.text: Open talks with Gargash Prime on last-mile and GCC delivery for the planned Dubai hub.

moves.title: Protect margin on B2C parcels
moves.text: Review marketplace and cross-border parcel rates where low-cost rivals like J&T are growing. Defend on service before cutting price.

note: Read from today's news. Check against our own numbers before acting.
